chapter: Early listening, piano and adolescent conflict
title: Playing pool and trying to win with honor
summary: Economic pressure led him into pool, where he was a poor loser but wanted to win honestly.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: pressure. You see, economics makes a person make decisions early in life that they might not normally make otherwise.
And so it makes it very easy to be enticed to get involved in some things that are not looked up as to be the better fields of endeavor.
Like for instance playing pool, you know.
I played pool at an early age that's what I'm saying. You see, I got thrown into that, you automatically get thrown into that.

Well, some of the people that I took money from seemed to think I was. I didn't -- I never considered myself to be a vicious competitor, but I never was a good loser. And I say this by saying that I never wanted to lose, and I would do everything in my power, that was legal, not to lose. And getting back, not trying to be boastful, or not trying to -- I'm being honest. As I said I still had this influence from my father, and I never considered myself suc-

cessful at cheating. And all these things I did, like playing pool, whatever, I always wanted to win with honor. And I've been in some situations where I've had a chance to cheat or steal, and many of my teachers or cohorts were expert thieves and you know, like the hand is quicker than the eye type. And I learned a lot of those tricks, but I used them only to protect myself. And I've always used that theory. Whether it's good or bad, I don't know, but I feel good about it, you know, that even then I always tried to use a way of honor, you know.
Yes. You knew you ought to be honest.
Well, I was taught that way, you know, let's put it that way.
